title: Runaway Atla-chan
text: “Anyway, got it… though I don’t exactly have meat on hand, so I suppose I’ll secure some from the magenta frogs around here in the labyrinth.”
“I’d appreciate that.”
“The thigh meat’s edible, if I recall.”
“……You two have gotten scarily nonchalant about counting magenta frogs as an ingredient now.”

Back when Ren and Itsuki were freshly summoned, they’d probably have flinched at that and suggested some other dish instead. Anyway, with that settled, cooking commenced. We used the shields and swords from the drops as cookware, I say. I handled the fire output and temperature control. This time, what Father whipped up was meatball hotpot, hamburger steaks, and curry-flavored sautéed dishes, all made from magenta frog thigh meat.
“Naofumi, I told you to skip the curry—my sense of smell’s gotten stronger.”
Ren was already munching away at the sauté.
“There’s no need to accommodate Ren’s complaints when he’s scarfing it down like that.”
“It really is light yet has a surprisingly deep flavor. They say frog meat resembles chicken, but with Naofumi-san’s cooking, that doesn’t bother me at all.”
“One Naofumi per household, that’s the ticket. If we’ve got Naofumi, maybe going to Naofumi’s world wouldn’t be so bad.”
“True. Aside from that, there doesn’t seem to be much novelty left, but as long as you feel like you’re time-traveling, there’s no problem.”
“‘No problem,’ she says. Wait, are we back on that topic?”
“Wasn’t it you, Naofumi-san, who said you wanted to visit Ren-san’s world? I don’t see why I can’t say the same back.”
That felt like a solid counterpoint, I must admit. Father’s world, was it… From what he’s told me, it’s nearly identical to my own world. Come to think of it…

“I recall hearing that Tiger Guy went to Father’s world once, I say. Something about Tiger Girl acting up something fierce over there, so he was brought along as a restraining influence. When he came back, I remember him talking about Father’s world.”
Yes, that’s definitely how it went. Tiger Guy had been going on about his trip to Big Brother’s world to everyone in the village.
“Fohl-kun did?”
“Atla-san being a handful… I genuinely can’t picture that from the two we know.”
“Yeah. I haven’t talked with her much, but Atla-chan seems like such a quiet kid. I can’t imagine her being selfish at all.”
“The tiger girl of the very first world was quite aggressive, I say. Enough to get into brawls with Tiger Guy.”
“I can’t picture that at all. This feels like one of those cases where you’d never notice the difference without looping through it.”
Is that so? I do think there’s a fair difference between the Big Sister of this loop and the one from the first world, though.
“About as much difference as between Black Thunder and Kuro-chan, I’d say.”
“No, that comparison doesn’t help either.”
“Probably it’s the gap between Naofumi-san’s usual self and Naofumi-san when angered… roughly the difference Motoyasu-san knew in the very first Naofumi.”
“That one’s easier to picture, given how Kou reacts when he gets you angry.”
“Somehow you’ve all reached a weirdly convincing consensus.”
Father scratched his head, looking troubled. Well, I could certainly understand the difference when it came to sheer terror.
“If you use Naofumi-san’s negotiating demeanor as the baseline, the gap becomes clear enough.”
“The duality of man, huh. Once the on-off switch breaks, you can perceive it as an entirely different person.”
“Anyway, back to the topic—Fohl-san went to Naofumi-san’s world, right? What kind of things did he talk about?”
“Specifically I’m curious about the food and his reactions to it.”
The scene of Ren and Itsuki questioning Tiger Guy came back to me. That time was…
“His energy was rather low, but Itsuki was asking Tiger Guy the things that Ren tends to worry about, I say.”
“Well, that’s bound to be a concern. Even with everything changed, I’m still me, so my curiosity would naturally itch.”
“I don’t think my world has anything particularly strange going on, though.”
“Tiger Guy said he was already used to eating Father’s cooking, so nothing seemed odd to him.”
Most of the food-related things were already things Father had been making all along, and plenty of it has been recreated in this world too.

“Well, it’s Fohl-san we’re talking about. Unlike us, he might not notice odd details… no, since it was an entirely unknown world to him from the start, it’d be hard for him to tell what’s strange anyway.”
“He apparently got quite excited talking about the cars. Said it surprised him how many there were, just driving around like it was nothing.”
“Well, in this world it’s mostly horse-carts or Filolials and other monsters people ride, so an ordinary car would be a rare sight.”
Those are the kind of things you’d only see around Faubrey or Shieldfreeden.
“So, about Fohl acting as the one to restrain Atla—what exactly happened there?”
“Apparently—in Father’s world, Tiger Girl turned out to be the daughter of some massive conglomerate, and she kept using her money to barge into Father and Big Sister’s life over and over.”
That much, I can easily imagine.
“I say, Motoyasu can easily imagine it, indeed. I’ve experienced school life with a wealthy pig more times than I can count.”
“Motoyasu-kun probably knows exactly how to deal with that kind of thing.”
“These days, if it gets truly bothersome, all it takes is a good verbal thrashing—but back when I was chasing after pig behinds, I was—well, utterly at their mercy.”

Thinking back on it now, it’s genuinely baffling why I ever put up with such a troublesome pig. There’s no doubt she was the type to sulk the moment things didn’t go her way. Come to think of it, back then… Father had been staring at me intently.
“There’s no point asking Motoyasu about this—it’ll probably just make things more troublesome.”
“Is something the matter?”
“Nothing. Just go look after the Filolials.”
If I had pushed my case a little harder back then, might I have gotten to visit Father’s world instead of Tiger Guy?

“The old Motoyasu-kun’s response to girls—well, pigs—was probably exactly as predictable as you’d expect… the type of soft-spoken guy who just silently takes a beating from some tsundere heroine, right?”
“Nowadays he’d probably retaliate without hesitation and beat them senseless.”
“We’d probably have to step in and stop him before things got recklessly dangerous.”
“Ha, pigs are creatures that resort to violence the moment things don’t go their way, I say. Sulk immediately and spread nasty rumors if you don’t apologize fast enough.”
I’ve heard plenty of times that she shows no mercy toward anyone who pulls that kind of stunt, myself included.
“Hypothetically, if I asked Motoyasu-kun for advice—like, ‘how should I go about persuading a runaway Atla-chan?’—what would you say?”

Hmm… so the premise is that it’s Father asking. If Father told me to do something about Tiger Girl, then… given that she’s the one who protected Father, Filo-tan, and Filolial-sama with her very life, I’d search for a way to restrain her while minimizing any injury, as much as possible. The complication is that the tiger girl of the first world existed as a translucent ghost-like being, so this only applies hypothetically, as if she were still alive. But assuming this is about Father wanting to resolve the matter—how would one deal with a tiger girl who keeps barging into the peaceful days shared by Big Sister and Father? Even when scheduling a date carefully in advance, that tiger girl has enough forcefulness and lack of self-control to crash right into Big Sister’s date day.
“Either let her do exactly as she pleases, or arrange for her to be constantly together with Big Sister at all times, I say.”
“……That’s basically just cutting her loose.”
“Enjoying a lively daily life through group activities is the correct answer, indeed. Whenever some event or gathering comes up, you go with whichever option Big Sister suggests.”
“Being nice to everyone while quietly raising the affection level of your favorite heroine—that’s the textbook definition of a gal-game protagonist.”
“Surely something will happen and she’ll suddenly settle down, or she’ll mysteriously stop appearing once another pig takes the spotlight.”
“That just sounds like ‘endure until you unlock the character-exclusive route’…”
For some reason, Father and the others let out a sigh. Whatever could be the matter, I wonder?
